input.quote: During the term and for twenty-four months thereafter, Customer shall not develop, market, sell, or acquire any product or service that competes with Vendor in any territory.
input.rationale: Section 12.4 (second instance) imposes an undefined-scope, all-territory, 24-month post-term non-compete on us — beyond the fallback and squarely in walk-away territory — and it contradicts Section 12.3, in which Vendor acknowledges no non-compete has been given. Deleted.

input.quote: Nothing restricts Customer from developing, acquiring, licensing, selling, or using any product or service, engaging any supplier, hiring any person who responds to general recruitment, or conducting business in any field or territory.
input.rationale: No exclusivity or sole-supplier obligation binds us; Section 12.3 expressly preserves our freedom to engage any supplier. The only quasi-exclusivity feature is the match/right-of-first-refusal in Section 7.2, which we have redlined under MFN rather than flagging the same term twice.

input.quote: Before engaging another provider, Customer must disclose and match for Vendor any more favourable commercial offer it receives.
input.rationale: Section 7.2 is an open-ended MFN running against us: we must disclose any more favourable third-party offer and give Vendor a match right before engaging another provider. That is walk-away territory (unlimited scope, no time limit, no comparison carve-outs) and it conflicts with Section 12.3's no-most-favoured-customer acknowledgement. Deleted; Vendor-granted MFN remains welcome.

input.quote: Customer shall not solicit, hire, or employ any Vendor employee during the term or for twenty-four months afterward, regardless of how the employee applies.
input.rationale: This is a one-sided 24-month no-hire covering every Vendor employee with no general-advertising or unsolicited-approach carve-out — beyond the fallback and expressly a walk-away item — and inconsistent with Section 12.3. Narrowed to a mutual 12-month non-solicit of personnel directly involved in the Services with the standard carve-outs and no no-hire.
